PullRequest.Title: sessions: Filter cloud history and surface linked issues
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Reduce stale cloud-session history and show which GitHub issues a cloud session is addressing.

- Add `github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.sessionVisibility`, defaulting to `30days`, with `24hours`, `7days`, `30days`, `90days`, and `all` options. There is no `none` option.
- Filter in the Copilot cloud provider using the Task API's most recent activity timestamp, before resolving pull requests or fetching changed files. Refresh on setting changes and cache expiry, and prevent obsolete requests from replacing fresh results.
- Fetch GitHub's structured PR-closing issue relationships and expose them as session artifacts and references for the existing GitHub issue pill. Deduplicate links and update or remove them atomically as metadata changes.

## Behavior and scope

Hiding sessions does not delete or archive them. `all` removes only the age limit; existing session and pull-request exclusions remain unchanged.

Issue detection uses verified GitHub relationships, not incidental PR-body mentions. Cross-repository public GitHub issues are supported; enterprise-hosted issues remain openable artifacts without public GitHub polling. Both PR lookup paths request up to 100 linked issues.

Verified example relationship: PR #336399 links issue #335868.

## Validation

- Client compile and type check: `npm run gulp compile-client`
- Copilot build: `npm run compile-copilot`
- Copilot extension TypeScript check
- Repository pre-commit hygiene, targeted ESLint, and `git diff --check`
- 56 Copilot provider/API unit tests passed
- 127 client provider/artifact unit tests passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed promotion line, default-visible consumer, one-model-per-key cache, REST boundary, and 15-minute cadence are all explicit. Only how often PRs link unusually many issues is uncertain, affecting severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent GitHub REST issue requests, response bytes/objects, and long-lived polling timers/models.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After URL deduplication the cost is linear in K distinct public closing issues, with K capped at 100 per PR. Cold activation performs K requests concurrently; warm activation within 60 seconds is coalesced, while a long-lived active session performs another request for each still-open issue every 15 minutes (conditional 304s still cross the network).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network I/O and API pressure from a large concurrent burst plus sustained polling.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Cloud sessions did not populate gitHubInfo.issues from PR-closing relationships, so opening an existing cloud session created no issue models and issued no per-issue REST refresh or polling traffic.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed adapter promotes every deduplicated public linked-issue artifact into gitHubInfo.issues. SessionChatInputToolbar consumes that array by creating one shared model per distinct issue, immediately calling refresh(), and starting polling for every issue not known to be closed whenever the Issues pill is enabled.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1295 appends every parsed public linked-issue artifact to the issues array that is returned in gitHubInfo; the same PR requests closingIssuesReferences(first: 100), so this newly populated array can contain up to 100 distinct references.
Findings.Title: Defer live polling for linked issues
Findings.Impact: Opening a cloud session whose PR closes many public issues now launches up to 100 GitHub REST requests off the UI critical path and keeps up to 100 open-issue pollers active, repeating that network fan-out every 15 minutes. This can contend with other GitHub features and consume API/network capacity even though the PR metadata already supplies the titles needed to render the pill.
Findings.Evidence: The Issues pill is visible by default (defaultHiddenKinds excludes Issues). Its autorun loops every issue ref, invokes model.refresh(), and starts polling in sessionChatInputToolbar.ts lines 388-404. GitHubIssueModel refresh calls GitHubIssueFetcher.getIssue, which performs GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}; each open issue then revalidates every 900,000 ms. The reference collection coalesces duplicate keys and refreshes within 60 seconds, but there is no aggregate limiter across distinct issues, so K unique links still produce K concurrent REST requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Render all references from the supplied URL/title metadata, but create and refresh live issue models only when the Issues dropdown or a specific hover is opened; if background state is required, cap or batch the subset that is polled rather than eagerly polling all 100.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The timer-to-refresh-to-extension-host-provide path and all expensive transitive boundaries are explicit in the repository. The exact number and clustering of user sessions is uncertain, which limits severity, but the repeated-work mechanism and quadratic relationship are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Task API calls plus per-session GitHub GraphQL PR lookups and REST PR-file/commit-comparison requests.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N visible sessions with distinct cutoff times, the timer rebuilds N, then N-1, and so on remaining enrichments: O(N^2) session-boundary work (up to 5,050 enrichments for the 100-item catalog), with each rebuild launching its remaining per-session operations concurrently via Promise.all.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated network bursts, excessive API I/O, and avoidable refresh latency as sessions age out.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change there was no exact per-session age cutoff timer. Enriched chat-session items remained cached until an existing provider refresh; the five-minute background check fetched the task catalog but only invalidated the enriched cache when its size changed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added expiry scheduler calls refresh() at the oldest visible session's exact activity cutoff. That clears the whole enriched cache and fires onDidChangeChatSessionItems; the extension-host bridge immediately invokes provideChatSessionItems again, which refetches the Task API catalog and re-resolves PR and changed-file metadata for every still-visible session before scheduling the next session's cutoff.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added callback at line 464 invokes this.refresh() whenever cachedSessionItemsExpiresAt passes; added lines 1497-1498 install the next per-session expiry after every rebuild, and filterCloudSessions computes that expiry as the minimum individual task expiry.
Findings.Title: Coalesce cutoff expiry instead of rebuilding every remaining session
Findings.Impact: With the Agents window open and many cloud tasks from a clustered work period reaching the 30-day cutoff, each individual task expiry causes another full concurrent GitHub enrichment burst for all remaining tasks. The list can contain up to 100 Task API results, so distinct expirations can produce quadratic repeated enrichment, consuming network/API quota and creating repeated list refresh latency.
Findings.Evidence: refresh() clears cachedSessionItems/chatSessionItemsPromise and fires the change event (lines 918-927). ExtHostChatSessions handles that event by immediately calling controller.refreshHandler, whose implementation calls provider.provideChatSessionItems. That method performs one backend fetch and Promise.all over the remaining sessions (lines 1428-1484), resolving each PR via GraphQL and then fetching PR files or a commit comparison via GitHub REST. The new tests at provider spec lines 423-441 explicitly establish that the timer fires a change event and the ensuing provide performs another backend fetch.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the raw/enriched catalog through age-only expiry and remove or hide expired cached items locally, scheduling the next cutoff without refetching unchanged PR/file metadata. Alternatively coalesce expirations into a bounded time bucket and reuse per-session enrichment across cutoff refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the cloud-session list with the default 30-day visibility filter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Task API catalog fetch must complete first; filtering then runs synchronously before per-visible-session PR resolution and changed-file retrieval. Promise.all waits for every visible session's enrichment before the list is returned, so all those network operations are on the list's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 100 cloud tasks globally, or one task-list request per workspace repository
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One global call in Agents/empty windows, otherwise one concurrent call per repository, plus at most one repository-id lookup per distinct unresolved repository ID during that fetch
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same task-list boundary already populated the cloud catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before filtering and list enrichment can begin

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each visible task's pull request through GraphQL, with possible open-PR search fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one direct lookup and one fallback search per visible task, launched concurrently; fallback search can return 20 PRs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already resolved PRs per listed task, including the same fallbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise.all waits for all visible task resolutions before returning list items

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch PR files or compare base/head commits for each visible task
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one REST request per visible task after PR resolution, concurrently across tasks
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already fetched changed files for every listed task; the new age filter beneficially avoids this for hidden tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The list waits for every changed-file request

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return up to 100 closing issue URL/title nodes nested under each GraphQL PR result
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 100 nested issue nodes per returned PR; a fallback search can return 20 PRs, though realistic PRs usually link far fewer issues
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same GraphQL calls omitted closing-issue nodes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded response bytes and parsing to the existing PR lookup on the list critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 100 tasks returned by the Task API, reduced to M visible tasks by the age filter. Each visible task can require one PR lookup and one PR-files or commit-comparison request; repository-id lookups are grouped per repository only within one catalog fetch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository-scoped Task API calls run concurrently per open repository. Visible-session enrichments run concurrently without a shared limiter via Promise.all. Requests for the same repository are not grouped for PR lookup or file retrieval.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm cached ChatSessionItems are returned until the earliest visible task's exact expiry. Filtering old tasks before enrichment reduces cold work. PR and file enrichment has no provider-level cache in the traced path; the backend repository-id promise cache lasts only for one fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the ordering, Promise.all fan-out, 100-task bound, and filter placement are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The typical visible-session count and number of closing issues per PR are not established. Filtering is a net improvement for old sessions; the bounded nested GraphQL payload alone was not reported separately because realistic magnitude is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding for ordinary cold/warm list loading: filtering occurs before expensive enrichment and reduces work. The exact-expiry invalidation behavior is analyzed separately and is reportable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible cloud sessions cross their individual activity cutoffs while the Agents window remains open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The expiry timer calls refresh(), and the extension-host event bridge immediately invokes provideChatSessionItems. The refreshed list cannot be published until a new Task API fetch and all remaining per-session PR/file enrichments finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch the complete Task API catalog on each age-only invalidation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog fetch per distinct task cutoff while the provider stays active
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-task expiry timer invalidated the catalog; background checks occurred every five minutes and did not clear enriched items unless the count changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks each refreshed list before filtering

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat PR resolution and changed-file retrieval for every still-visible task after each cutoff
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N + (N-1) + ... + 1 session enrichments across N distinct expirations, up to 5,050 for 100 sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The enrichment path existed, but the diff newly invokes it at each individual age cutoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each expiry-driven list refresh waits for the full concurrent enrichment burst

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N visible sessions with distinct expiry timestamps, up to the 100-item task catalog. Work is especially bursty when tasks created during one work period expire close together.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Expirations are serialized by one earliest-expiry timer, but each expiry starts a new full-catalog rebuild whose remaining M session enrichments run concurrently without a limiter. The next precise expiry schedules after that rebuild.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The timer clears the complete enriched cache rather than retaining unchanged items. There is no reuse of PR/file enrichment across successive age-only invalidations. Each successful rebuild schedules the next task's precise cutoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added timer, cache clearing, automatic extension-host refresh, and transitive boundaries are directly traced and covered by tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may not keep the Agents window active through many clustered cutoffs, and many catalogs contain fewer than 100 visible sessions. This lowers severity but does not affect the deterministic repeated-work mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated network work: precise per-item expiration causes quadratic full-catalog enrichment instead of a local age-only update or coalesced refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an active cloud session whose pull request closes public GitHub issues
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session and pill can render from the supplied URL/title metadata. Live issue refreshes are started asynchronously and are off the direct UI critical path, but they compete for network/API resources immediately after activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET each linked issue's live details from /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent request per distinct public linked issue on cold active-session activation, up to 100
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud sessions did not publish issue refs, so this consumer created no issue models or requests for PR-closing issues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the direct render critical path, but creates an immediate shared-network/API burst

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate every still-open linked issue using ETags
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per open issue every 15 minutes while the Issues pill remains enabled for the active session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No linked-issue pollers existed for cloud-session PR relationships.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work, not required for chat progress

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K distinct public github.com issue URLs after linkKey deduplication, with K capped at 100 by the GraphQL query. Enterprise-hosted links remain artifacts and do not enter this polling path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The reference collection coalesces identical owner/repo/number keys and duplicate refreshes share one promise, but all K distinct models call refresh concurrently with no aggregate limiter. Each open issue owns an independent 15-minute poll scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold models perform one full REST request. Live or recently restored models suppress on-demand refreshes for 60 seconds; up to 100 disposed snapshots retain ETags and data. Conditional 304 polling still performs network I/O. Closed issues stop polling after their state is fetched; unresolved/failing issues retry when reactivated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: metadata promotion, default Issues-pill visibility, model acquisition, REST request, coalescing rules, and polling interval are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most PRs likely close only a few issues, while umbrella PRs can approach the 100-node cap. Uncertain prevalence limits severity, not the proven K-request burst and polling cadence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: already-titled references eagerly create up to 100 live REST fetches and persistent pollers instead of resolving details on interaction.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event clears the item cache and the extension-host bridge immediately reloads the catalog. The new visibility value is applied after the Task API fetch and before PR/file enrichment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload Task API catalog and enrich sessions visible under the new setting
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full reload per user configuration change, with per-visible-session PR/file boundaries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The setting and its reload event did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to publish the newly configured list

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single user setting action over up to 100 tasks, reduced to the selected age window before enrichment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One reload per configuration event; remaining session enrichment uses the same unbounded Promise.all behavior as normal list loading.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Changing the setting cancels the prior expiry timer and invalidates cached items. Switching to all yields an infinite expiry and no timer; switching to a bounded window installs a timer for the earliest visible session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the listener and refresh path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Setting changes are infrequent and user initiated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: one reload is proportionate to an explicit setting change, and filtering before enrichment avoids unnecessary per-hidden-session calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Translate linked-issue metadata into artifacts and references during session updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Parsing, validation, deduplication, artifact construction, and reference construction are synchronous during adapter creation/update, before observables publish the new session metadata.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 100 linked issue records per cloud PR; duplicate normalized URLs are removed before artifact/reference construction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded linear processing; no boundary calls in the adapter itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each session update rebuilds arrays, but equality checks suppress unchanged observable publication. URL normalization deduplicates within the session; no cross-session artifact cache is needed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loops and 100-node upstream cap are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Metadata updates and 100-link PRs are uncommon; allocation and URI parsing are bounded and small relative to the downstream network work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No standalone CPU/allocation finding. The linear bounded translation is reasonable; only its promotion into eager live issue polling is reportable.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and relevant transitive provider, extension-host, GitHub model, cache, and network paths. Submitted two medium-severity findings: per-cutoff full-catalog rebuilds with quadratic repeated enrichment, and eager up-to-100 linked-issue REST refresh/poll fan-out. Ordinary age filtering before enrichment is beneficial, setting-change reload is proportionate, and bounded metadata translation alone is not a regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
